sections.heading: Bio
sections.body:
I am a historian of the long nineteenth century, working primarily on labour, migration and the institutions that recorded both. My first book traced the paper trail of a single port town across sixty years; my current project asks what happens to a community's history when its archive burns.

I teach undergraduate and graduate seminars at Greenhill University, and I supervise doctoral work on archival theory, memory studies and the social history of the British Atlantic.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
PhD, History - University of Edinburgh, 2009. Dissertation on port labour and municipal record-keeping, supervised by Professor M. Adeyemi.

MA, Modern History - King's College London, 2004.

BA (Hons), History - University of Delhi, 2002.

sections.heading: Employment
sections.body:
Professor of History, Greenhill University - 2019 to present.

Associate Professor, Greenhill University - 2013 to 2019.

Lecturer in Modern History, University of Bristol - 2009 to 2013.

Visiting Fellow, Institute of Historical Research - 2016, 2021.
